hints: Because the car travels at constant speed on a horizontal road, the driving force equals the resistance force: $F_D = 750\text{ N}$.
Use $P = F_D v$ with $F_D = 750\text{ N}$ and $v = 32\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and convert watts to kilowatts.
walkthrough:
Since the car travels at constant speed, the net force is zero so the driving force equals the resistance:
$$F_D = 750\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power developed by the engine using $P = F_D v$:
$$P = 750 \times 32 = 24000\text{ W} = 24\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the equilibrium condition for motion at constant speed on a horizontal road: when acceleration is zero, the forward driving force $F_D$ must exactly balance the opposing resistance $R$:
$$F_D = R = 750\text{ N}$$

State the power formula relating driving force and velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute $F_D = 750\text{ N}$ and constant speed $v = 32\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 750 \times 32 = 24000\text{ W}$$

Convert the result to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$:
$$P = \frac{24000}{1000} = 24\text{ kW}$$

hints: Calculate the new engine power: $24\text{ kW} - 8\text{ kW} = 16\text{ kW} = 16000\text{ W}$.
Find the new driving force at the instantaneous speed of $32\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $F_D = \frac{P}{v}$.
Apply Newton's second law $F_D - 750 = 1250a$ to find the acceleration and state the deceleration as a positive value.
walkthrough:
Find the reduced engine power and the corresponding new driving force at $v = 32\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P_{\text{new}} = 24 - 8 = 16\text{ kW} = 16000\text{ W}$$
$$F_D = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{16000}{32} = 500\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally with car mass $m = 1250\text{ kg}$ and resistance $750\text{ N}$:
$$F_D - R = ma$$
$$500 - 750 = 1250a$$
$$-250 = 1250a \implies a = -\frac{250}{1250} = -0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

State the magnitude of the instantaneous deceleration:
$$\text{Deceleration} = 0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Newton's Second Law: Finds new driving force $F = 500\text{ N}$, forms $500 - 750 = 1250a$ to get $a = -0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and states deceleration is $0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the new power of the engine after the sudden decrease of $8\text{ kW}$:
$$P_{\text{new}} = 24\text{ kW} - 8\text{ kW} = 16\text{ kW} = 16000\text{ W}$$

State the formula for driving force at instantaneous speed $v = 32\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{16000}{32} = 500\text{ N}$$

State Newton's second law in the forward direction of motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$F_D - R = ma$$
Substitute $F_D = 500\text{ N}$, resistance $R = 750\text{ N}$, and mass $m = 1250\text{ kg}$:
$$500 - 750 = 1250a$$
$$-250 = 1250a$$

Solve for acceleration $a$:
$$a = -\frac{250}{1250} = -0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The negative acceleration signifies a slowing down, giving an instantaneous deceleration of $0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

hints: Find the component of the car's weight acting down the incline: $mg\sin\alpha = 1250(10)(0.096)$.
At constant speed, the driving force equals the sum of the non-gravitational resistance and the weight component down the slope: $F_D = (1000 + 8v) + 1250(10)(0.096)$.
Form the power equation $P = F_D v = 60000\text{ W}$, set up a quadratic equation in $v$, and solve for the positive root.
walkthrough:
Calculate the component of weight opposing upward motion along the inclined plane with $\sin\alpha = 0.096$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\alpha = 1250(10)(0.096) = 1200\text{ N}$$

Since the car travels up the incline at constant speed ($a = 0$), the driving force balances total resistance:
$$F_D = (1000 + 8v) + W_{\parallel} = 1000 + 8v + 1200 = 2200 + 8v$$

Apply the power relation with $P = 60\text{ kW} = 60000\text{ W}$:
$$P = F_D v$$
$$60000 = (2200 + 8v)v$$
$$8v^2 + 2200v - 60000 = 0$$

Divide by $8$ and factorize the quadratic equation:
$$v^2 + 275v - 7500 = 0$$
$$(v - 25)(v + 300) = 0$$
Since speed must be positive:
$$v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Forms driving force $F = 2200 + 8v$, equates $(2200 + 8v)v = 60000$, and solves the quadratic equation to obtain $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

teacher_walkthrough: Identify all forces acting on the car parallel to the inclined road. As the car moves uphill, both the non-gravitational resistance and the component of weight act downhill.

Calculate the component of weight parallel to the slope:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\alpha$$
Substitute $m = 1250\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\sin\alpha = 0.096$:
$$W_{\parallel} = 1250 \times 10 \times 0.096 = 1200\text{ N}$$

Add the speed-dependent resistance to find the total resistance force:
$$R_{\text{total}} = (1000 + 8v) + 1200 = 2200 + 8v$$

Because the car travels at constant speed, acceleration is zero, so the engine driving force $F_D$ must equal the total resistance:
$$F_D = 2200 + 8v$$

State the power equation relating driving force, velocity, and power:
$$P = F_D \times v$$
Substitute $P = 60\text{ kW} = 60000\text{ W}$:
$$60000 = (2200 + 8v)v$$
Expand the right-hand side:
$$60000 = 2200v + 8v^2$$
Rearrange into standard quadratic form:
$$8v^2 + 2200v - 60000 = 0$$

Simplify the quadratic equation by dividing every term by $8$:
$$v^2 + 275v - 7500 = 0$$
Factorize the quadratic expression:
$$(v - 25)(v + 300) = 0$$
This gives two mathematical solutions: $v = 25$ or $v = -300$. Because speed must be non-negative, discard the negative root:
$$v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
